jobs.title: Vice President of Finance And Operations
jobs.description:
Employment Type:
Full-Time
Location:
Greater Toronto Area, ON (Hybrid)
Industry:
Professional Services
Position Type:
New Role

About the Opportunity

This newly created VP, Finance & Operations role reporting directly to the Founder & CEO. You’ll own profitability, cash, the people function, legal and risk, and the operating plan the company runs against.
You’ll have a direct line to the founder, clearly defined decision rights, and room to shape the team beneath you.

Key Responsibilities

Finance & Profitability

Lead the finance function and build the team beneath you, delivering a close, reporting and controls the leadership team trusts, along with statutory compliance and tax remittances
Manage gross and contribution margin by service line, client and team, inside a pricing and margin framework you design, with rate cards, discount thresholds and a floor below which work is declined
Find and close margin leakage, and make numbers-backed recommendations on where to invest, what to reprice and what to stop
Own cash and working capital, including a rolling cash forecast reliable enough for hiring and investment decisions, DSO, collections, client credit terms and banking relationships
Work with the technology and data lead to move finance reporting toward real time, automate manual processes and choose the long-term finance tools

Planning & Strategy Execution

Turn the CEO’s strategy into a rolling 24-month operating plan with owners, dates and resourcing
Design and own the company scorecard and KPI framework, in the format you propose
Catch deviations early and build recovery plans directly with business leaders, so issues reach the CEO already diagnosed
Build the business cases and resourcing models for new hires, new functions and new service lines

Legal, Compliance & Risk

Oversee legal and compliance with external counsel, including client, vendor and employment agreements, privacy obligations and disputes
Own the insurance program and a live enterprise risk register

People & Culture

Lead people and culture through a senior People & Culture lead, building a development path that gets new hires productive faster and a defined way to identify and keep top performers
Make role clarity standard across the firm, so every role has defined outcomes, decision rights and escalation triggers

Office of the CEO

Run the leadership team’s weekly, monthly and quarterly operating rhythm, with decisions logged and every action owned
Present results to the firm and act as the CEO’s thinking partner, with written recommendations and constructive challenge

What You Bring

10+ years of progressive finance experience, including 5+ as head of finance with ownership of operations, and a degree in accounting, commerce or business
A finance and operations function you built rather than inherited, ideally while the business was changing how it delivers or who it sells to
Experience as a planning partner to a CEO or owner, including disagreeing constructively and defending your recommendations with data
A track record of moving margin, not just reporting it, with results you can quantify
Cash and working capital management across more than one revenue model, including a cash forecast that leaders rely on
People leadership in a headcount-driven business, including owning HR or acting as its business partner
Oversight of contracts and risk in a company without in-house counsel
Hands-on use of AI tools or automated workflows to solve business problems
Working command of Canadian statutory requirements, including CRA, GST/HST and Ontario employment standards

Nice to Have

CPA designation
Experience in a founder-led or owner-managed company, after time inside a larger organization
A professional services or SaaS background
Organization design experience

Next Steps

We do appreciate all interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.
Clarity Recruitment is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible recruitment process and workplace. If you require accommodation, please let us know in advance and we will work with you to meet your needs.
Please note: We use AI-assisted tools for notetaking during the screening process.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
SearchLabs has been exclusively retained to Partner with rybka Group Inc. on a multitude of different roles and opportunities across the Country. rybka Group Inc. is a leading Canadian consulting engineering firm that specializes in mechanical, electrical, and commissioning engineering services for the built environment. Headquartered in Markham, Ontario, the firm was formed in 2025 through the strategic merger of two legacy engineering firms: rybka Group Inc., established in 1913, and Ellard-Willson Engineering Limited, founded in 1954. This merger unites over a century of combined expertise, a shared commitment to human-centric design, and a passion for sustainable, innovative engineering solutions.

Who is rybka Group Inc.:

rybka Group Inc. stands at the forefront of building services engineering, offering comprehensive solutions across a broad spectrum of sectors, including:
Commercial and residential developments
Healthcare and long-term care facilities
Educational and institutional buildings
Hospitality and cultural venues
Retail and Food Services
Critical Systems

rybka Group Inc. believes in the power of Perpetual Building Engineering, an approach that integrates sustainable thinking at every stage of a building’s lifecycle. By blending engineering precision with architectural vision and environmental stewardship, their work contributes to healthier, more resilient communities. A family 1st ethos, rybka Group is not only looking to be the firm of choice across all building sectors across all disciplines (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural, and Commissioning), but is looking to build the most positive/productive work environment second to none.

Heritage and Innovation:

rybka Group brought to the merger a distinguished history of pioneering projects in Toronto, including Maple Leaf Gardens and the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Ellard-Willson Engineering contributed a strong track record in institutional and public infrastructure, with work reaching as far back as the original CN Tower.
This deep-rooted legacy informs their forward-thinking practice, ensuring clients benefit from both proven experience and progressive design.

Director of Finance (Professional Services / Engineering Consulting)

Role Overview

rybka is seeking an experienced Director of Finance to provide financial leadership and oversight across the organization.
As a mechanical and electrical engineering consulting firm, our financial performance is closely connected to project delivery, utilization, billing, work-in-progress (WIP), accounts receivable, project profitability, and effective cash flow management. The Director of Finance will work closely with the CEO, Managing Principal, Principals, Project Managers, and administrative team to strengthen financial controls, improve visibility into business performance, and support informed decision-making.
This is a hands-on leadership role suited to an individual who can operate strategically while remaining actively involved in the day-to-day financial management of the business

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Planning

Lead the company's overall finance and accounting function and provide financial guidance to senior leadership.
Develop and maintain annual budgets, forecasts, cash flow projections, and financial plans.
Provide the CEO, Managing Principal, and Principals with clear and timely financial reporting and analysis.
Identify financial risks, trends, and opportunities and recommend appropriate actions.
Support strategic planning, financing initiatives, banking relationships, and other corporate financial matters.
Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support business and operational decisions.

Project Financial Management

Provide financial oversight of the firm's engineering projects, including project budgets, WIP, revenue recognition, billing, utilization, and profitability.
Work closely with Principals and Project Managers to review project financial performance and identify projects that are over budget, under-billed, delayed, or otherwise financially at risk.
Establish consistent project financial planning, forecasting, and reporting practices across the firm.
Monitor project performance against fee proposals, contracts, budgets, and approved scope.
Support leadership in understanding project margins, resource allocation, write-offs, and financial performance by project, client, and business area.

Cash Flow, Billing & Accounts Receivable

Maintain short- and medium-term cash flow forecasts and provide leadership with clear visibility into the company's liquidity requirements.
Oversee the billing cycle and ensure invoices are issued accurately and on a timely basis.
Lead accounts receivable monitoring and collection strategies in collaboration with Principals and Project Managers.
Monitor aging reports, outstanding receivables, and collection risks.
Oversee accounts payable and payment planning while balancing operational requirements and cash flow priorities.
Maintain effective relationships with the company's banks, lenders, and other financial partners.

Accounting & Financial Reporting

Oversee month-end and year-end close processes and ensure accurate and timely financial reporting.
Review balance sheet reconciliations, income statements, cash flow reporting, and supporting schedules.
Maintain appropriate accounting policies, procedures, internal controls, and approval processes.
Coordinate with external accountants, auditors, tax advisors, payroll providers, and other professional advisors.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting, tax, statutory, and corporate reporting requirements.
Oversee corporate filings, remittances, and other financial compliance obligations.

Systems, Processes & Controls

Provide financial leadership for Deltek Vision and related accounting and project-management systems.
Improve the quality and consistency of financial data, project setup, billing information, WIP reporting, and project forecasting.
Develop and document finance policies, procedures, approval authorities, and internal controls.
Identify opportunities to automate and streamline financial and administrative processes.
Establish reliable management dashboards and KPIs for leadership.

Payroll, Benefits & Administration Oversight

Provide financial oversight of payroll processing and related reconciliations.
Ensure payroll changes, deductions, remittances, and financial reporting are properly controlled.
Work collaboratively with HR on compensation budgeting, benefits costs, vacation liabilities, staffing forecasts, and other people-related financial matters.
Provide financial oversight of insurance premiums, leases, professional services, and other significant corporate expenditures.

Leadership & Business Partnership

Act as a trusted financial partner to the CEO, Managing Principal, and Principals.
Translate financial information into practical business insights for non-financial leaders.
Establish accountability around budgets, project performance, billing, collections, and financial commitments.
Support Principals in understanding the financial impact of staffing, project delivery, business development, and operational decisions.
Lead, mentor, and develop members of the finance/accounting team.
Promote a culture of financial discipline, accountability, and timely decision-making across the organization.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
CPA designation required.
Approximately 8–12+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including senior financial leadership responsibilities.
Experience within an engineering consulting, architecture, construction, professional services, or project-based organization is strongly preferred.
Strong understanding of project accounting, WIP, revenue recognition, utilization, project profitability, and professional-services billing.
Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, financial reporting, and internal controls.
Experience working directly with senior executives, business owners, and operational leaders.
Experience with Deltek Vision required.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and financial modelling.

Compensation and Benefits

Base Salary Range 140k to 150k
Paid Benefits
Paid Vacation
Employee Shared Options Program

Artificial Intelligence and Recruitment Transparency

Our recruitment and selection process is conducted by people, not artificial intelligence. We do not use AI to screen, assess, rank or select applicants. All applicants are reviewed and evaluated by our human recruitment team.

Please send your resume to jboose@searchlabs.ca

jobs.title: Director, Finance, HR and Operations
jobs.description:
Brion Raffoul
is a leading IP boutique law firm in Canada, situated in Westboro, Ottawa. Our exceptional team is passionate about helping innovative companies protect their ideas, designs and brands worldwide. Our clients include domestic and multinational companies, government agencies, as well as universities.

We are seeking a Director, Finance, HR and Operations
to join our operations on a full-time basis. Reporting directly to the Managing Partner, the Director will be responsible for managing the full scope of the company’s financials, including the day-to-day accounting operations, and for leading the firm’s human resources and day-to-day operations. The ideal candidate will bring a positive, hands-on approach and must be comfortable with problem-solving and managing multiple priorities at once, holding staff accountable and following tasks through to completion without reminders. This is a terrific opportunity to take full ownership of a senior role while working directly with the Managing Partner to help shape the future of the business.

As a member of the management team, the Director will contribute to strategic planning, ensure compliance with legislative requirements, and provide leadership to staff, the Managing Partner and Management Team. The role also supervises and mentors a team of 20 to support daily operations. The Director is the first point of contact for all staff matters and manages people directly: setting clear expectations, giving timely feedback, and addressing performance and policy issues.

Key Responsibilities:

Human Resources & People Management
Lead all HR operations for the firm’s staff, including recruitment, onboarding, training, performance management and departures.
Own the full employee life cycle: a written training plan in place before each new hire’s first day; 30, 60 and 90-day check-ins; and structured departures (notices, systems access, equipment, firm announcements).
Hold staff accountable: set clear expectations, deliver regular substantive feedback, and address performance and policy issues (including attendance and work-from-home policies) directly and promptly.
Plan and maintain a firm-wide training calendar and track completion.
Review timesheets, expense claims and other staff submissions for completeness and accuracy before they reach the partners.
Oversee payroll, benefits, group health insurance and RRSP programs, employment contracts and employee records.
Onboard contractors and outsourced staff, confirming equipment, systems access, confidentiality agreements and schedules in writing before the start date.
Maintain HR policies and the employee handbook, and advise leadership on employment standards, health and safety, human rights and other legislative compliance.
Promote a respectful, equitable, and inclusive workplace culture.

Financial Management & Accounting
Lead all financial operations, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and compliance with GAAP.
Oversee accounts payable/receivable, payroll, and general ledger functions.
Prepare, and analyze monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements and reports.
Review all reports and calculations for accuracy and completeness before distribution.
Work with the IP Manager and administrative staff so work is invoiced at a regular cadence through the month, avoiding month-end backlogs.
Manage cash flow, banking relationships, and investments.
Coordinate the annual audit and liaise with auditors and the Financial Institutions.
Complete all statutory filings, including CRA returns, HST, EHT and payroll remittances.
Maintain and strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and procedures.

Budgeting & Financial Planning
Lead the annual budgeting process with the Managing Partner.
Provide forecasts, variance analyses, and recommendations to support informed decision-making.
Plan and lead finance system changes, such as an accounting software migration, with a written project plan, timeline and staff training.

Administrative Leadership & Supervision
Supervise and mentor staff members (Administrative & Accounting Support, Reception & Office Support)
Provide coaching and professional development to enhance team skills and performance.
Ensure effective daily operations, workflow coordination, and clear communication across the administrative team.
Oversee reception and office upkeep (supplies, cleaning, deliveries) with regular checks, so issues are caught and resolved without partner involvement.
Improve administrative processes, systems, and tools for operational efficiency.

Facilities & Operations Management
Oversee building operations and maintenance, working with contractors and suppliers, and following up on repairs through to completion.
Manage service agreements for Security, HVAC, and other ad hoc maintenance contracts.
Lead risk management and insurance review processes.
Ensure compliance with safety regulations and workplace health and safety standards.
Develop and implement facilities and operational continuity policies.

Information Technology & Systems
Oversee IT systems, data security, and technology operations with support from external IT consultant
Plan and manage technology upgrades and infrastructure improvements as required
Support digital transformation efforts to enhance efficiency and data integrity.
Use AI and automation tools to streamline reporting and administrative work.
Manage the annual IT budget.

Organizational Support & Collaboration
Participate in organizational strategy, planning, and reporting as part of the management team.
Provide financial and administrative guidance to the Executive Team.
Support communications and marketing initiatives.
Foster collaboration and effective communication across all departments.
Represent the organization in external meetings as required.

The ideal candidate
is an experienced and technically strong financial, HR and administrative leader who brings a solid foundation in accounting, budgeting, human resources and organizational operations. You bring strong hands-on accounting experience (10+ years), ideally within a profit-oriented professional services environment, including at least 5 years leading HR and managing people directly. With strong analytical skills, sound judgment, and a commitment to continuous improvement, you excel at turning complex financial information into clear insights to the Executive Team. You are an effective people manager who holds people accountable, fosters collaboration, supports staff growth, and builds positive relationships across the organization. Highly organized and detail-oriented, the candidate demonstrates strong communication skills, adherence to best practices, and a deep commitment to equity, inclusion, and community values. You read carefully, check your own work before it goes out, ask the right questions before acting, and manage multiple priorities without needing reminders.

What Makes a Candidate Stand Out:

Holds or is actively pursuing a CPA designation and brings advanced proficiency in QuickBooks and Excel.
Holds or is pursuing a CPHR designation or equivalent HR training.
Demonstrates successful experience leading finance and administration, including preparing budgets, operational accounting, cash flow management & financial reporting.
You bring strong hands-on accounting experience (10+ years) and a proven record in HR, operations, or administrative leadership.
Experience in a law firm, patent agency or other professional services firm, including disbursement accounting, is a strong asset.
Shows a proven track record of improving systems, processes, and organizational efficiency across finance, HR, IT, and facilities operations.
Brings strong communication skills and the ability to convey technical information with clarity to diverse audiences.

jobs.title: IT Director (Digital Operations)
jobs.description:
About Sonance Financial

Sonance Financial launched in October 2026, bringing together founder-led advisory firms in Lethbridge, Ottawa, Edmonton and Phoenix. We are building one operating model and one modern technology platform, and we need an experienced technology leader to make it work across every office.

About the role

As our first in-house technology leader, the IT Director (Digital Operations) is a hands-on role. You will be the bridge between our people and our managed IT services partner: you'll turn business needs into clear requirements, solve problems directly, and hold vendors to a high standard. You will also lead our first practical steps with AI and own our IT and AI policies. This is a chance to build technology at a growing wealth firm from the ground up, with a clear path to Head of Technology as we grow.

Reporting to the CEO on an interim basis. You will work closely with the Director of Integrations, the Director of Support Services and the Chief Compliance Officer. The role has no direct reports at launch.

What you'll do

IT operations and managed services:
Own the relationship with our managed IT services partner, including escalations, invoices and monthly service reviews. Troubleshoot hands-on across devices, networks, Teams calling and meeting rooms.
Identity, SSO and client portal:
Roll out Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on with MFA for all users. Support the launch of our client portal and resolve login issues. Run joiner, mover and leaver processes and quarterly access reviews.
Partner firm onboarding:
Build a repeatable playbook so every new office is fully working on day one. This covers device setup, Microsoft 365 email and file migration, platform access, and retiring legacy systems.
Platform vendors:
Oversee our wealth-management platforms (CRM, portfolio accounting, financial planning, ERP and related tools), keep vendor oversight records, and evaluate new tools.
AI enablement:
Work with an outside consultant to pilot practical AI workflows and scale the ones that work. Make sure each one is signed off by Compliance, and keep an inventory of AI tools.
Security, continuity and policy:
Run our information security program with our IT partner, including the annual risk assessment, vulnerability testing, incident response and staff training. Test our business continuity and disaster recovery plans every year, maintain the IT and AI policy framework, and provide evidence for audits and due diligence.
Strategy and budget:
Keep a rolling technology roadmap, manage the technology budget, and report progress to leadership.

What success looks like in your first year

The client portal is live with single sign-on.
A clear support model is in place with our IT partner, with SLA reporting every month.
Our IT and AI policy framework is approved and covered in staff training.
We have a full inventory of systems, vendors and licences, plus a 2–3 year technology roadmap.
Two or three AI pilots have been delivered, with measured results.

What you bring

5+ years in IT or technology management, including oversight of managed service providers and vendors.
Hands-on Microsoft 365 administration (Exchange Online, SharePoint, Entra ID, Intune) and experience implementing SSO.
A track record of delivering migrations from start to finish.
Working knowledge of security frameworks (NIST or CIS), incident response and business continuity planning.
Knowledge of Canadian privacy and record-keeping requirements for financial services, such as PIPEDA and securities regulator expectations.
A genuinely AI-forward mindset, balanced with good judgment about risk.
A calm, clear communicator who can support people across several offices and time zones.

Nice to have

Experience in wealth management or other regulated financial services.
Familiarity with wealth platforms such as CRM, portfolio accounting, custodian integrations and client portals.
A degree in Computer Science or Management Information Systems, or equivalent experience.

The details

Full-time, permanent. This posting is for an existing vacancy.
Hybrid, based in Ontario (Greater Toronto Area preferred), with up to about 20% travel to our offices.
Base salary range: $130,000 – $180,000 CAD per year, depending on experience.
Sonance Financial does not use artificial intelligence to screen, assess or select applicants for this position.

Apply here: https://ats.rippling.com/sonance-financial-inc/jobs/04f35c65-4600-424a-8418-6e383ed8228e

Sonance Financial is committed to an inclusive, accessible hiring process. If you need an accommodation at any stage, let us know and we will work with you.

new_jobs.title: Director, Finance, HR and Operations
new_jobs.description:
Brion Raffoul
is a leading IP boutique law firm in Canada, situated in Westboro, Ottawa. Our exceptional team is passionate about helping innovative companies protect their ideas, designs and brands worldwide. Our clients include domestic and multinational companies, government agencies, as well as universities.

We are seeking a Director, Finance, HR and Operations
to join our operations on a full-time basis. Reporting directly to the Managing Partner, the Director will be responsible for managing the full scope of the company’s financials, including the day-to-day accounting operations, and for leading the firm’s human resources and day-to-day operations. The ideal candidate will bring a positive, hands-on approach and must be comfortable with problem-solving and managing multiple priorities at once, holding staff accountable and following tasks through to completion without reminders. This is a terrific opportunity to take full ownership of a senior role while working directly with the Managing Partner to help shape the future of the business.

As a member of the management team, the Director will contribute to strategic planning, ensure compliance with legislative requirements, and provide leadership to staff, the Managing Partner and Management Team. The role also supervises and mentors a team of 20 to support daily operations. The Director is the first point of contact for all staff matters and manages people directly: setting clear expectations, giving timely feedback, and addressing performance and policy issues.

Key Responsibilities:

Human Resources & People Management
Lead all HR operations for the firm’s staff, including recruitment, onboarding, training, performance management and departures.
Own the full employee life cycle: a written training plan in place before each new hire’s first day; 30, 60 and 90-day check-ins; and structured departures (notices, systems access, equipment, firm announcements).
Hold staff accountable: set clear expectations, deliver regular substantive feedback, and address performance and policy issues (including attendance and work-from-home policies) directly and promptly.
Plan and maintain a firm-wide training calendar and track completion.
Review timesheets, expense claims and other staff submissions for completeness and accuracy before they reach the partners.
Oversee payroll, benefits, group health insurance and RRSP programs, employment contracts and employee records.
Onboard contractors and outsourced staff, confirming equipment, systems access, confidentiality agreements and schedules in writing before the start date.
Maintain HR policies and the employee handbook, and advise leadership on employment standards, health and safety, human rights and other legislative compliance.
Promote a respectful, equitable, and inclusive workplace culture.

Financial Management & Accounting
Lead all financial operations, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and compliance with GAAP.
Oversee accounts payable/receivable, payroll, and general ledger functions.
Prepare, and analyze monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements and reports.
Review all reports and calculations for accuracy and completeness before distribution.
Work with the IP Manager and administrative staff so work is invoiced at a regular cadence through the month, avoiding month-end backlogs.
Manage cash flow, banking relationships, and investments.
Coordinate the annual audit and liaise with auditors and the Financial Institutions.
Complete all statutory filings, including CRA returns, HST, EHT and payroll remittances.
Maintain and strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and procedures.

Budgeting & Financial Planning
Lead the annual budgeting process with the Managing Partner.
Provide forecasts, variance analyses, and recommendations to support informed decision-making.
Plan and lead finance system changes, such as an accounting software migration, with a written project plan, timeline and staff training.

Administrative Leadership & Supervision
Supervise and mentor staff members (Administrative & Accounting Support, Reception & Office Support)
Provide coaching and professional development to enhance team skills and performance.
Ensure effective daily operations, workflow coordination, and clear communication across the administrative team.
Oversee reception and office upkeep (supplies, cleaning, deliveries) with regular checks, so issues are caught and resolved without partner involvement.
Improve administrative processes, systems, and tools for operational efficiency.

Facilities & Operations Management
Oversee building operations and maintenance, working with contractors and suppliers, and following up on repairs through to completion.
Manage service agreements for Security, HVAC, and other ad hoc maintenance contracts.
Lead risk management and insurance review processes.
Ensure compliance with safety regulations and workplace health and safety standards.
Develop and implement facilities and operational continuity policies.

Information Technology & Systems
Oversee IT systems, data security, and technology operations with support from external IT consultant
Plan and manage technology upgrades and infrastructure improvements as required
Support digital transformation efforts to enhance efficiency and data integrity.
Use AI and automation tools to streamline reporting and administrative work.
Manage the annual IT budget.

Organizational Support & Collaboration
Participate in organizational strategy, planning, and reporting as part of the management team.
Provide financial and administrative guidance to the Executive Team.
Support communications and marketing initiatives.
Foster collaboration and effective communication across all departments.
Represent the organization in external meetings as required.

The ideal candidate
is an experienced and technically strong financial, HR and administrative leader who brings a solid foundation in accounting, budgeting, human resources and organizational operations. You bring strong hands-on accounting experience (10+ years), ideally within a profit-oriented professional services environment, including at least 5 years leading HR and managing people directly. With strong analytical skills, sound judgment, and a commitment to continuous improvement, you excel at turning complex financial information into clear insights to the Executive Team. You are an effective people manager who holds people accountable, fosters collaboration, supports staff growth, and builds positive relationships across the organization. Highly organized and detail-oriented, the candidate demonstrates strong communication skills, adherence to best practices, and a deep commitment to equity, inclusion, and community values. You read carefully, check your own work before it goes out, ask the right questions before acting, and manage multiple priorities without needing reminders.

What Makes a Candidate Stand Out:

Holds or is actively pursuing a CPA designation and brings advanced proficiency in QuickBooks and Excel.
Holds or is pursuing a CPHR designation or equivalent HR training.
Demonstrates successful experience leading finance and administration, including preparing budgets, operational accounting, cash flow management & financial reporting.
You bring strong hands-on accounting experience (10+ years) and a proven record in HR, operations, or administrative leadership.
Experience in a law firm, patent agency or other professional services firm, including disbursement accounting, is a strong asset.
Shows a proven track record of improving systems, processes, and organizational efficiency across finance, HR, IT, and facilities operations.
Brings strong communication skills and the ability to convey technical information with clarity to diverse audiences.

new_jobs.title: IT Director (Digital Operations)
new_jobs.description:
About Sonance Financial

Sonance Financial launched in October 2026, bringing together founder-led advisory firms in Lethbridge, Ottawa, Edmonton and Phoenix. We are building one operating model and one modern technology platform, and we need an experienced technology leader to make it work across every office.

About the role

As our first in-house technology leader, the IT Director (Digital Operations) is a hands-on role. You will be the bridge between our people and our managed IT services partner: you'll turn business needs into clear requirements, solve problems directly, and hold vendors to a high standard. You will also lead our first practical steps with AI and own our IT and AI policies. This is a chance to build technology at a growing wealth firm from the ground up, with a clear path to Head of Technology as we grow.

Reporting to the CEO on an interim basis. You will work closely with the Director of Integrations, the Director of Support Services and the Chief Compliance Officer. The role has no direct reports at launch.

What you'll do

IT operations and managed services:
Own the relationship with our managed IT services partner, including escalations, invoices and monthly service reviews. Troubleshoot hands-on across devices, networks, Teams calling and meeting rooms.
Identity, SSO and client portal:
Roll out Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on with MFA for all users. Support the launch of our client portal and resolve login issues. Run joiner, mover and leaver processes and quarterly access reviews.
Partner firm onboarding:
Build a repeatable playbook so every new office is fully working on day one. This covers device setup, Microsoft 365 email and file migration, platform access, and retiring legacy systems.
Platform vendors:
Oversee our wealth-management platforms (CRM, portfolio accounting, financial planning, ERP and related tools), keep vendor oversight records, and evaluate new tools.
AI enablement:
Work with an outside consultant to pilot practical AI workflows and scale the ones that work. Make sure each one is signed off by Compliance, and keep an inventory of AI tools.
Security, continuity and policy:
Run our information security program with our IT partner, including the annual risk assessment, vulnerability testing, incident response and staff training. Test our business continuity and disaster recovery plans every year, maintain the IT and AI policy framework, and provide evidence for audits and due diligence.
Strategy and budget:
Keep a rolling technology roadmap, manage the technology budget, and report progress to leadership.

What success looks like in your first year

The client portal is live with single sign-on.
A clear support model is in place with our IT partner, with SLA reporting every month.
Our IT and AI policy framework is approved and covered in staff training.
We have a full inventory of systems, vendors and licences, plus a 2–3 year technology roadmap.
Two or three AI pilots have been delivered, with measured results.

What you bring

5+ years in IT or technology management, including oversight of managed service providers and vendors.
Hands-on Microsoft 365 administration (Exchange Online, SharePoint, Entra ID, Intune) and experience implementing SSO.
A track record of delivering migrations from start to finish.
Working knowledge of security frameworks (NIST or CIS), incident response and business continuity planning.
Knowledge of Canadian privacy and record-keeping requirements for financial services, such as PIPEDA and securities regulator expectations.
A genuinely AI-forward mindset, balanced with good judgment about risk.
A calm, clear communicator who can support people across several offices and time zones.

Nice to have

Experience in wealth management or other regulated financial services.
Familiarity with wealth platforms such as CRM, portfolio accounting, custodian integrations and client portals.
A degree in Computer Science or Management Information Systems, or equivalent experience.

The details

Full-time, permanent. This posting is for an existing vacancy.
Hybrid, based in Ontario (Greater Toronto Area preferred), with up to about 20% travel to our offices.
Base salary range: $130,000 – $180,000 CAD per year, depending on experience.
Sonance Financial does not use artificial intelligence to screen, assess or select applicants for this position.
